In India, there are many discount offers available, allowing people to get great phones at affordable prices. 24:55 I think there's a slight misunderstanding here and as a sworn keyboard warrior set out to change the word, I HAVE TO LET OUT THIS RANT.

Turning on DLSS renders your game at a lower native resolution and then upscales it using Al. For example, game resolution lai 4k ma set gareko chha, with DLSS turned on vane gpu le 1440p ma render garchha game lai and then upscales it to set 4k resolution target with AI, meaning it's not true native 4K. This obviously reduces graphics quality, especially if you set DLSS to Ultra Performance (contrary to how some might associate "Ultra Performance" with the best possible graphics quality). However, it gives you a significant FPS boost since the GPU is rendering fewer pixels natively. Setting DLSS to Quality, on the other hand, boosts your FPS with minimal quality loss.

Bahini ta dalli raixa ta
LG is better when it comes to clothes care. It washes clothes very delicately without damaging them whereas in Samsung it's not guaranteed. Turbowash models in LG and bespoke models in Samsung save washing time but LG supports all programmes whereas Samsung doesn't. 

Samsung has a soak option which is great as it makes detergent like creamy foam. Really nice.

If LG model doesn't have turbo-wash, then it's more or less like Samsung only.

LG doesn't drain the detergent if we change our mind and switch to other programmes. Samsung drains everything away. 

Samsung is a tiny bit energy efficient. LG stops spinning and balances the load if it detects a bit of shakiness while Samsung simply continues.

In Samsung you can change rinse times while it's in wash mode and spinning levels while it's in wash and rinse mode but in LG, you have to hit pause and then change. 

I like LG turbowash only because of its flexibility and fabric care.

Need more expensive gaming pc builds
For a beginner pc builder, please dont use this as a reference to help in your build. As she is more experienced it might look easy but there are some tips there:

1. Put essentials only before putting the motherboard inside the casing(RAM, CPU, SSD, AIO cooler)
2. Don't put psu inside the case first as it will only hinder you while doing the Cable Management. 
3. There should be more intake fan than exhaust fan. A positive pressure is always better than negative pressure. It will/may harm your motherboard and all the components with dust particles.
4. Before putting everything in place do a test run with the main components and gpu outside the casing so that everything works out fine.
5. While it is not a needed step, while you are using your motherboard place a switched on psu box only near you and whenever you are going to touch the motherboard touch the psu first. It will transfer the electric current built up in your body to the psu and your motherboard will not be damaged. 
6. More thermal paste is always better than less thermal paste. 
7. If you have a glass casing, please place the glass near or to a safe and steady place.
8. If you are going for the same level of performance, then you can get a better deal within 2.3lakhs. b650 motherboard is good and is also a little futureproofed too.
9. Never and i mean never cheap out on a psu. always buy well rated and higher wattage psu.
10. Also if you just want more native fps on gaming focused build then it might be better to use rx 9070xt as a gpu. Elsewhere nvidia is always better.

### OnePlus 13R
- **Display:** 6.74 inches, AMOLED, 120Hz
- **Processor:** Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1
- **RAM:** 8GB/12GB
- **Storage:** 128GB/256GB (non-expandable)
- **Camera:** Triple rear camera (50MP + 12MP + 2MP), 16MP front camera
- **Battery:** 5000mAh, 100W fast charging
- **OS:** OxygenOS based on Android 13

### Honor 200 Pro
- **Display:** 6.78 inches, OLED, 120Hz
- **Processor:** MediaTek Dimensity 9200
- **RAM:** 8GB/12GB
- **Storage:** 256GB (non-expandable)
- **Camera:** Triple rear camera (200MP + 12MP + 2MP), 32MP front camera
- **Battery:** 4800mAh, 100W fast charging
- **OS:** Magic UI based on Android 13

### Samsung Galaxy A56
- **Display:** 6.4 inches, Super AMOLED, 120Hz
- **Processor:** Exynos 1380
- **RAM:** 6GB/8GB
- **Storage:** 128GB (expandable via microSD)
- **Camera:** Triple rear camera (50MP + 12MP + 5MP), 32MP front camera
- **Battery:** 5000mAh, 25W fast charging
- **OS:** One UI based on Android 13

### Nothing Phone 3A
- **Display:** 6.55 inches, AMOLED
- **Processor:** Snapdragon 7 Gen 1
- **RAM:** 8GB/12GB
- **Storage:** 128GB/256GB (non-expandable)
- **Camera:** Dual rear camera (50MP + 50MP), 16MP front camera
- **Battery:** 4500mAh, 45W fast charging
- **OS:** Nothing OS based on Android 13

### Vivo V5
- **Display:** 5.5 inches, IPS LCD
- **Processor:** MediaTek MT6750
- **RAM:** 4GB/5GB
- **Storage:** 32GB (expandable via microSD)
- **Camera:** 13MP rear camera, 20MP front camera
- **Battery:** 3000mAh, 18W fast charging
- **OS:** Funtouch OS based on Android 6.0 (may be outdated)

### Summary
- **Performance:** The OnePlus 13R and Honor 200 Pro are likely to outperform the others in terms of processing power due to their higher-end chipsets.
- **Camera:** The Honor 200 Pro has the highest megapixel count, making it potentially the best for photography.
- **Battery:** Both the OnePlus 13R and Samsung Galaxy A56 have large batteries and good charging capabilities.
- **Design & Software:** OnePlus and Samsung typically offer a more polished software experience, while the Nothing Phone aims for a unique aesthetic.
- **Price:** This can vary widely based on the region and configuration.

### Conclusion
Your choice should depend on your specific needs, such as camera quality, performance, battery life, and software preference. If you're looking for the best overall performance and camera, the OnePlus 13R or Honor 200 Pro would be strong contenders. For a balanced mid-range option, consider the Samsung Galaxy A56. If you want a unique design, the Nothing Phone 3A is an interesting choice, while the Vivo V5 may feel outdated compared to the others.

Love your vedio
I want to address the biased review. Just because a phone has a large amount of RAM and a decent processor doesn’t automatically make it fast. What truly matters is how well the company optimizes the phone’s software and manages multitasking. Many companies put powerful processors in low-budget phones for marketing, but this doesn’t always result in better performance. Brands like Samsung offer superior processing power and smoother multitasking, even with lower-end processors, because they focus on balancing hardware and software. So, when reviewing or sponsoring phones, it's important to consider the overall performance, not just specs.

i think The Vivo X200 Pro is a powerhouse smartphone camera, blending portability, advanced tech (like its 200MP lens and computational photography), and solid performance for most users. But it can’t fully replace a DSLR due to its smaller sensor, limited image quality, lack of lens flexibility, and reduced control in professional scenarios. DSLRs remain the gold standard for photographers who prioritize quality, versatility, and creative freedom over convenience. That said, for everyday photography or enthusiasts who don’t need pro-level gear, the Vivo X200 Pro is an incredible alternative that bridges the gap impressively & in phone there is not only camera use the Ui and the user-friendly phone.

Guys, Samsung A16 5g 8/256 variant leko maile falgun ma. 

1. Yo phone lastai jhur chha hai nalinus. Kineko 2 months Mai table ma rakhirakheko thaun ma aafai screen blackout vayera display gayo.
2. Camera ni ramro chhaina,    picture ma details chhaina. Blur blur nikalxa jatti gare ni. 
3. Network tipdaina ramrarii. Aru phone le tipda yesma ali ali matra tipxa. Malai kasaile phone garda samparka huna sakena vandine raixa jailei.
3. Speaker vayena, sano aawaj chha. 
4. Battery chhitai drain hune raixa. Charge ta redmo ko half time jatti matra tikxa.
5. Design le farak pardaina vanera leko, aile yo hjr aama le chalaune jasto phone dekkhine vayera ali standard thaun ma hat ma liyera hidna sakirako chhaina. Goji mai hunxa.

Not a bad build tara Nepal ma 1.5 lakh kharcha garera ni kasto average gaming pc matra banne. 

4060 nai chalaune ho bhane Ryzen 7700 ko kam nai chaina. 7600 liye huncha, 10k bach cha. Ajja Aliexpress bata 7500F 18k ma paincha kosailai tya bata kinne idea cha bhane. 

NVME ni assadhai overpriced eta. Gaming matra nai garne ho bhane SATA SSD linus 1 TB ko at least ani baira bata 1TB nvme 10k ma line pachi milda.

RAM sake samma 32 GB halnus 20k bhitra but aile mildai mildaina bhane pachi thape huncha.

Yadi paisa bachyo bhane boru RTX 3080 2nd hand liye huncha (80k) jati ma. 

Radeon ko graphics card haru k saro overpriced ho eta. 7900 GRE 60k-70k ma uthauna paye Kati majja authyo.

Nepal ma price to performance pauna impossible cha. Sake samma motherboard, monitor, case matra brand new kinne eta. Aru ta sab anta bata or 2nd hand kinnu thik. 

Competitive gaming garnu huncha bhane Liye huncha 144hz with 4060 RTX tyo ni valo, cs matra khelna. Triple A gaming ko lagi stable 144+ fps 4060 bata pauna ki dlss ki settings na ghataye kaam chaina. Pachi upgrade garne sochdai kinne ho 😂

I think the chances of PWM dimming triggering headaches are increased in *low brightness* rather than *high brightness*
It has to do with the duty cycle of PWM, which at the highest brightness is 100%, which means PWM frequency is at the highest advertised level. It decreases proportionally to changes in brightness percent which might make the flickering noticeable for some.

Summery: 

1. **Success of Nepali Brands**: Nepali mobile accessories brands like Alma, Ultima, and Kick are currently successful and profitable, competing against large Indian brands by offering similar products at competitive prices.

2. **Challenges Ahead**: Despite their current success, Nepali brands may fail in the long run due to the superior quality and features of international brands, which could outcompete them if they enter the Nepali market at competitive prices.

3. **White Labeling Limitations**: Many Nepali brands rely on white labeling products from Chinese manufacturers, which limits their ability to offer unique and high-quality products. Simply rebranding these products is not sustainable.

4. **Need for Innovation**: To sustain their success, Nepali brands need to invest in research and development, hire skilled engineers, and improve product quality rather than focusing solely on marketing and pricing strategies.

5. **Government Support and Economic Impact**: If Nepali brands can improve their product quality and receive support from the government, it would benefit the national economy by retaining foreign exchange reserves, creating local jobs, and boosting the income of Nepali engineers, workers, and retailers.

Why are other chipsets slightly underpowered than snapdragon?

2. Chahine vanda dherai type ko chipsets. Ex. Dimensity 700, 1100, g80, g90, 9000,. exynos 1200, 1100, etc...

3. Different types of cpu architecture (3nm 4nm 6nm 12nm

Just wanted to share some thoughts on Asta Wolf's defense, even though I'm against everything they did.

Regarding them being a Nepali OEM brand:
In their OBJECTIVE, they have clearly stated, 'For now, it will be importing the products but as a long vision, it shall be designing, manufacturing and assembling all the products by itself in Nepal for Nepalese and for the rest of the globe as well.' This is a good future prospect; hope they do start manufacturing soon.

About fake marketing, tech scams, and the product description not matching the actual product:
They might have been scammed by the seller about the product description. They probably copy-pasted the entire description they found. They do that copying thing a lot, lol. Fun fact: they even copied their company's 'terms and conditions' from Chat GPT. (checked with zeroGPT cus had doubts)

About the 'Designed in Nepal' label:
I think they meant the box is designed in Nepal, lmao.

Anyway, they should have tested the product quality before blindly launching it with such aggressive marketing. It was definitely good for business, but if they continue this, I don't see Asta Wolf on the list of Nepal's OEM brands in the long run.

P.S. I am not affiliated with Asta Wolf in any ways.😂

4:18 yo phone ma ufs 2.1 storage haina emmc 5.1 aunxa.  For those who dont know, read speed of eMMC 5.1 tops at 250 MB/s and on the write side of things around 125 MB/s . Whereas the UFS 2.1's storage read speed is around 750 MB/s and for write is 150 MB/s. Makes a huge difference in device performance.
It's Emmc5.1 storage type. Not ufs 2.1

As a Level 51 XP owner myself, I will have to correct some of the claims made in this video. Some of the *_misinformation_* in this video are:
1. The screen covers *_150%_* *_of_* *_the_* *_sRGB_* *_spectrum,_* not 98%. The depth in color is apparent even to the naked eye.
2. The control feature is called 'SystemX', not X6. Pretty sure the people from Level 51 would have informed you about that when you received the unit.
3. The body of the laptop is completely made of *_Full_* *_Metal_* *_Alloy._* It's definitely not plastic. So, I have no idea how you could've gotten that wrong when the unit is cold to the touch.
4. There are dedicated and separate microphone/headphone jacks. It's definitely not combo audio jack.
5. There are *_no_* *_3070ti_* *_options_* *_available_* on the website. However, there is a RTX3080Ti 16GB option. Please, double check with your sources.

Some other issues I noticed with the video:
1. Why are you guys not including any details regarding the software used to graph the gaming performance?
2. With GadgetByte being one of the leading tech-info companies, you could at least afford a *_Thermal_* *_Imaging_* *_Camera,_* right? What's with the body temperature scanner pointed towards the screen? *_Show_* *_the_* *_angles_* *_right._* Point to the spots where the heat is being dissipated or generated.
3. The graphic design used to portray the function of Integrated GPU and Dedicated GPU is vague enough for a normal consumer to be mislead. Even in the dedicated GPU mode, the use of colors in battery life consumption should be opposite. How did you mix that up?
4. This brand is not an OEM brand. As far as I'm aware, they call it a custom laptop supplier.

The more of your videos I take a look at, the lower my expectations get. *_Stop_* *_following_* *_the_* *_script_* *_that_* *_strictly._* Get your research right. Fix your claims and do better. *_This_* *_video_* *_is_* *_literally_* *_a_* *_second-hand_* *_embarrassment_* *_for_* *_the_* *_Nepali_* *_tech_* *_community._*

Edit: Though this laptop can game pretty well and has decent specs, it's more catered towards creators and workstations. So, maybe explaining in that terms would be better. :D

Lenovo legion 5 or nitro 5
Never buy a laptop for gaming. Save and go for a full fledge desktop PC. Same generation Core i9 on a laptop gets clapped by a core i5 of a Desktop. Even the mobile GPU in a laptop isn't as powerful as a dedicated GPU. Laptops aren't upgradable except the ram or SSD. You can refresh CPU and GPU on your desktop after a couple of years but that's a dead end on a laptop. Only thing that's an advantage on a laptop is that you  can carry it around.

frest
Hello everyone, we didn't mean 125Hz polling rate is great for gaming. We meant that the mouse is great for someone gaming on a tight budget. Of course, for seasoned gamers, the 8ms delay is noticable compared to 1ms on a mouse with 1000Hz polling rate. But keeping the price in mind, it's a beginner mouse so someone going for such an inexpensive mouse will obviously not use it for competitive gaming with super high fps. Overall, it's not an endgame mouse it's just a mouse to kick start your journey into "gaming".

ramro dio
Since I have experience with drones and own a Mini 3 Pro, I recommend the Mavic Air 2s if you're considering purchasing a drone. As she mentioned, the price is about the same, and the air 2s is superior to the mini pro in every way besides weight. The reason the mini lineups were created was so that you could fly your drone in various US and European countries without a licence or aviation registration if it weighed less than 250 grammes. However, regardless of the size of your drone, you must register it in Nepal. So buy the Mavic air 2s if you live in Nepal and don't have any plans to travel to the US or Europe.

I've been using this phone in India for around 4 months now and there are some negatives and positives I'd like to share so that someone who is considering buying this phone could get an idea before their purchase. 

Cons:-
4G Connectivity is not good, but okay. Connection is not constant. Many times I have to switch it to 3G so that I could at least watch videos without buffering. I tried using my 4G sim in a different phone and it works just fine, so I think it's something to do with in 2b's 4G bands.

Don't buy this phone for cameras. They will do the job but not social media worthy. Good for pdf scans.

Speakers are nice and loud, but the placement is not good. You have to keep in mind not to cover it while listening to music or watching videos.

Even though software is good, I haven't received a single update ever since buying the phone.

Some minor petty gripes is that GPay has some issues. It does work, makes payments and does transfers perfectly. But while entering the password, the numeric buttons are not aligned properly. GPS also doesn't work great because lack of compass sensor. It only comes with 10w charger (it doesn't matter to me because I charge my phone overnight).

Pros:-
Great display for the price. Good brightness.
Great performance.
Good build quality.
Good battery life.
Type-C port.

!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!GUIDE TO BUILD A PC IN 2022!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

-single channel ram are almost unacceptable these days for that pc. It has enough slots. Should have atleast included another 4gb ram. 12 gigs dual channel is not that far from 16 gigs. 
-if you got money should definitely buy 256 sata ssd or 1tb hdd + 256 nvme ssd for C drive.
-1650ti has significant performance, infact any ti version of a graphics card is significantly faster than its normal version. like 1060 & 1060ti, 1660 and 1660ti etc
-for intel cpu, all of it has gen and another significant number. 
for eg-  lets take intel i5-10400. it means its the 10th gen(10,000) + 4th edition(400). there are mainly 3 basic scenarios
	#1 different cpu
	we all say i7 is better than i5 but its not true in all cases. i5 10400 is smoother than i7 8200. so always go for highest gen and highest edition possible, if you have choice.

	#2 same cpu different gen 
	i5 9800 will be smoother than i5 10,200

	#3 same cpu same gen different edition
	i5 8800 is smoother than i5 8250
-case of a pc is just a place to hold everything, the main thing you need is well ventilation. apart from that nothing else matters in casing. but choose a quality power supply like they did in the video. dont use the one provided on the box, infact if you can exchange it in the shop you are buying do it without a second thought.
-let me be honest unless you are a professional editor then you probably wont be able to distinguish between the trueness(idk if its a real word or not) of colors anyway. so for a monitor pick a decent 144hz monitor.  its been a standard even in many laptops since few years. 
-dont be shy to go 5-10% of your estimation. you probably wont be building another one anytime soon.

Speedtest shouldn't be done like that.
It's seen usually that in Chrome browser or any other browser , download speed is always low compare to dedicated software's / apps made for download only.If u download files from same server in Chrome and in Internet Download Manager , there will be significant difference.Chrome is an browser made to download , surf internet, use online application, etc. So, the Ram consumption will be higher and Memory writing rate will get slow down plus the optimisation of Chrome to download is not good.So, using Internet Download Manager to test download speed is better option. 
Plus , to test upload speed using terminal is better option. U can setup rclone remotes of any cloud service and use it to upload and download as well. I also don't recommend using OneDrive to use for download/upload speed test as their download / upload speed always fluctuates. Google drive is always an better option. And for proper upload test use rclone and for download , IDM.

When it comes to P2P, u were using public tracker where speed always fluctuate and even if files were well seeded, there were 54 peers as i seen in video so data transfer was splitted into 54 users so that could be reason u didn't get bit more/peak speed.I prefer to test using well seeded file in private tracker with tons of seeds bcz most files there are seeded using high speed seedboxes.

Using any usenet client (prefer NZBGET) config. without ssl connection and good news server is another best way to check download speed.

Video was good but hope to see some changes in future.Have a good day ahead.

Internet service providers harule internet to speed dekhauda "Mbps" use garxan. Yedi "Mbps" ko "b" lower case ma xa vane tyo vaneko "Mega bits per second". Jaba hami afno computer, mobile ma kei download, upload garxau tesma "MBps" use hunxa, capital "B" xa vane "Mega Bytes per second". 1 Mega Bytes per second (MBps) = 10 Mega bits per second (Mbps). So, sabai internet provider haruko internet speed lai 10 le divide garda actual speed tha hunxa. CG le 120 Mbps ko provide gareko xa that means 120÷10=12, so yo video ma steam bata game download garda max 12MBps pugya thyo. 12MBps vanda speed kaile bardaina, rarely max 13, 14 MBps pugna ni sakxa.

For ppl wondering what is NAT: I will try to explain my best in few sentences :DDDDD 

NAT: network address translation is basically a firewall, translating public network IP to a private network IP meaning - If you are browsing net through your phone, your phone will be given a public IP address for example: 66.23.5.1 which is equals to "Elon Musk" who is known to public - private IP address is like a students name "John Doe" who only the master of the class "Router" knows. So, if there is 4 devices connected then 4 devices will have 4 different IP's 

However, NAT is used in such a way to prevent exploiting multiple IPv4's and I quote "IPv4's" - So, basically, your router will be assigned public IP of 66.23.5.1 and through the router you will then be assigned private IP's such as 1.1.2.3 , 1.2.3.4 etc - This will prevent overcrowding IPv4 which can only take roughly 4 billion IPs. 

Why NAT ? It's very important in internet world however, it can break internet sometimes especially in gaming world:
NAT has 3 types: strict, moderate, open
ISP's in Nepal mostly use moderate or strict.

1. Strict (Type 3): While being secured, name defines how strict this is - It's like a prison cell and defined as mostly useless in gaming world. ( connected through a router )
2. Moderate (Type 2): This is mostly ideal to choose from all 3 of them as far as I am concerned. ( Connected through a router )
3. Open (Type 1): While being convenient and alot of benefits - This has alot of risks - Since, you are opening your doorway freely to enter all kinds of monsters on your network. So, open has it's own benefits and place but not everywhere. ( The system is connected directly to the Internet with own public IP address. )

I didn't want to criticize the Nepali OEM brand, but this laptop has too much heat as shown in the video.
95 degree Celcius on CPU is bad, even 85 degrees on GPU is also bad. The main reason of poor thermals is that is it thin and doesn't have proper fan and heat-sink pipes. The heat will also affect other components.

Do not buy this laptop for gaming, however you can buy it for office work, coding and other tasks.

LEGIT SUGGESTION.
Don't buy laptops in Nepal.  Find someone, friends/family/relatives who are abroad and buy from USA or someplace where the product price is low. Nepal ma jun laptop ni overpriced xa compared to what u can get outside. I bought Asus ROG strix G15 advantage edition from USA for 2lakhs (1650$). You can look abt that laptop in google or YouTube. 
Point is i managed to buy a laptop that can compete with highest end laptop out there for just 2 lakhs. Nepal ma 2lakh ma comparatively dherai unimpressive laptop hunxa. Specs nai chitta nabujne hunxa. So just a kind advice. Itti ko website ma 2lakh ko gaming laptop search garera, maile kineko sanga compare garda pani hunxa for reference. 
Just a kind advice for people who are planning to buy in nepali stores.

3. Heating 45°c pugxa matra messanger 2 minutes video call garo bhanne jann pub g haru khelo bhanne ta sochnus k hunxa hola ma sanga photo pani xa tara comment ma share garna mildena reixa
4.aaru ta yestai ho mobile charge garda sudha 46°c pugxa k bhako ho yesto 
5. Touch sensitivity problem bati gako thiyo ani offline game khelum vaneko ani ludo khele ko touch nai chaldena ani facebook ma pani scroll garxu left side ma hunxa right ma hudaina 
6. Speaker xanata dual speaker xa tara kamm xaina yesto sharp aauxa kann futla jasto ani thulo sound bhayo bhanera medium banauxu sunidai sundaina
7. Selfie camera nokia ko tik tike ma ramro aauxa hola boru testo xa
8. App crash pani hunxa maile messenger ma share gareko video herdai thiye ani back garxu ta video pani aauxa 
9. Build quality cheap xa yo bhanda ramro ta oppo a5s xa mero kasam
10. Amoled display ho tara k garnu aakha dukhe marnu hunxa khai maile m21 pani chalaye khai kei bhayena m21 samsung ko kasto ramro punchy xa vibrant
11. Mimi software ko ta kura na garum bug matra xa na update nai dinxa yo bhanda samsung ko one ui 10000000* ramro hola
12. Boru processor ra back camera chita bujdo xa
Conclusion:- specification ko paxadi na hunnu hola ma jasto tapai dherai paxutaunu hunxa

Had this for almost a month https://www.youtube.com/post/UgkxAxiUS5CgVC3j8FwNOHt037zhsquGQpXv  and I haven't had any major issues with it. I bought this to have another screen to stream or browse and it's great for this purpose. Compared to my iPhone there's sometimes a slight lag but that seems to be common for tablets at this price point. I wouldn't recommend it for use at work or school, and it doesn't have the capability to be used with a stylus for writing or drawing or anything but it's great if you aren't planning on using it as a primary device. The battery is good, under heavy use (6+ hrs a day) I need to charge it every other day but with light use you can go 4-5 days between charges. Overall a solid product and I'm happy with my purchase.

Macbook pro only has an extra GPU core which doesn't make any significant difference also 100 nits brighter display doesn't matter if you use it indoors. Also the so called studio speakers and microphones in mac pro are not much different that the ones in macbook air. Macbook pro also has the touch bar which is a personal preference. Mac pro has a slightly bigger battery which doesn't make much difference in battery life when compared to the air and the fan slightly helps to the sustain load but it's only 10-15% faster .So in my opinion these small improvements doesn't justify the $300 larger pricetag (for the base varient) and the increased thickness as well. You'll be better off buying either the 16GB Ram version or the 512gb storage version of macbook air rather than buying the macbook pro

It’s like you buy 4K Tv but your channel are HD channels.
For better connection create a networking mess. I use 1gigabit switch that goes to 3 repeaters in my house one is set for top floor one for my room that and one for general. I have 30mbps and I have capped the lobby router to 1mb/s each for each user i.e 8096mbps per user. This will help to eliminate network congestion. Among 3 routers the router placed in the lobby is 5ghz. Most of the devices I and my family use support 5ghz and it is good for video calling but don't get fooled by worldlink marketing that router does not cost 10k its more like 5-6k if you can find and do some research. All my wifi names are the same and the device auto switch to the strongest point in the house. Just keep in mind to check open channels in your area and set each router separate channel. This requires some networking knowledge too.

I just watched your 7t unboxing on YouTube, I also bought OnePlus 7t from Amazon 8/256gb, but I am facing display issues which is called green tint, I just wanted to know if all OnePlus 7t have these problem or I got defective one, please check on your phone and let me know


To check green tint issue:

1st- turn on dark mode

2nd- set screen brightness 10 to 20%

3rd- turn off room light (its visible only in dark)

4th- open chrome and then New Incognito Tab


Now check on notch area if its greenish or some abnormal colour, if its there then issue is there on display


If its grey dark as rest of display then no issue

I get all of that, but I also get that this design looks tired in 2020. There are many comparably priced Android phones that have managed to reduce their bezels. That’s not just an aesthetic consideration, either. Smaller bezels mean you can fit a bigger screen in a smaller phone body.

The bezels are a bother, but the build quality is not. Apple’s long history with this phone design means that it’s rock-solid. There’s no flex, no gross seams, no gaps. The 4.7-inch LCD display is as good as ever, with True Tone to help color-match your surroundings.

It’s an iPhone, and there’s a comforting sense of familiarity to it.

For those of you hanging on to the original iPhone SE in the hopes that Apple would make another small phone: I acknowledge you and your sadness. This is simply the way phones are these days. I will say it’s a very common experience for people to resist bigger screens and then love them when they finally give in, but that may not be yours. If it helps (it won’t), there aren’t any good tiny Android phones right now either.

As with the iPhone 7 and 8, the home button isn’t a physical button, but simply a spot on the bottom that gives you a tactile tap back when you press it. Please suggest a budget video editing laptop
I have used this model for around six months and let me point out some issues:
1) Nitro sense app is not optimized well. Once the fan starts to kick in, it doesn't settle down even if the temperature is back to normal. I had to manually update it from nitro-sense cool boost option.
2) Battery life is pretty good at first but after some plug and play gaming sessions for a week it will come back to around 3-4 hours of normal use.
3)  There is no support for legacy boot option. Also we cannot change the boot option from RST premium to SATA or AHCI and if anyone wants to install linux on the primary m.2 nvme ssd, you are doomed. I had to buy extra SATA ssd for that.
4) The dust buildup inside the laptop is terrible . I check around every two months and the amount of dust buildup is not good.
5) The touchpad gestures stop working periodically. Once to twice a day i have to disable and enable the touchpad using fn+f7 fot it to perform normally. I dont know how much it affects other people but once you start using touchpad for multitasking and configure advanced touch pad gestures it pisses me off when it doesn't work.

For me the biggest issue is the unoptimized NItro Sense app.
But given the price range you have to be ready for those compromises.
